evidence.claim: Electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) produce neutron stars with significantly lower natal kick velocities compared to iron core-collapse supernovae due to reduced asymmetric mass ejection.
evidence.relevance: Directly models hydrodynamical kicks in ECSNe, showing that the gravitational tug-boat mechanism yields low kicks (< 50 km/s) for ECS progenitors, distinguishing them from typical CCSNe.

evidence.claim: Neutron stars formed in ECSNe from super asymptotic giant branch stars may receive significantly lower kicks than typical neutron stars, leading to a population of wide binary pulsars.
evidence.relevance: Links low-kick ECSNe to observable populations of wide binary pulsars, providing a statistical signature for distinguishing ECS remnants in young populations.

evidence.claim: Observations of binary pulsars and pulsars in globular clusters require a subset of pulsars to have received weak natal kicks (< 50 km/s) at birth, consistent with ECS origins.
evidence.relevance: Provides observational constraints on kick velocity distributions, supporting the existence of a low-kick channel distinct from standard iron core-collapse.

evidence.claim: The gravitational tug-boat mechanism explains neutron star kicks as a consequence of asymmetric mass ejection, which is less pronounced in electron-capture supernovae due to their lower ejecta masses and energies.
evidence.relevance: Establishes the physical mechanism linking progenitor structure (low-mass ECS vs high-mass CCS) to the magnitude of the natal kick.

evidence.claim: Low-mass core-collapse supernovae (8-12 solar masses), which include ECS progenitors, have distinct nucleosynthetic yields and spectral signatures compared to higher-mass iron core-collapse events.
evidence.relevance: Identifies spectroscopic differences in nebular phases that can serve as additional observable signatures for distinguishing low-mass progenitors.

proposal.problemStatement: Distinguishing electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) from iron core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in young neutron-star populations remains challenging due to overlapping observational features. A robust observable signature is needed to identify the low-kick, low-mass progenitor channel of ECSNe.
proposal.rationale: ECSNe originate from super asymptotic giant branch stars (8-10 solar masses) with degenerate O-Ne-Mg cores. Unlike iron core-collapse, ECSNe have lower explosion energies and smaller ejecta masses. The gravitational tug-boat mechanism dictates that natal kicks are driven by asymmetric mass ejection; therefore, the reduced asymmetry and mass in ECSNe result in significantly lower kick velocities (< 50 km/s) compared to typical CCSNe (> 200 km/s). This difference in kinematic properties provides a clear statistical signature in young neutron-star populations.
proposal.technicalDetails: We will analyze the transverse velocity distribution of young radio pulsars (< 10 Myr) in the Galactic disk. By isolating pulsars with characteristic ages < 10 Myr and measuring their proper motions via VLBI or Gaia astrometry, we can reconstruct their natal kick velocities. We will compare this distribution against population synthesis models that incorporate both ECS and CCS channels with distinct kick distributions.

datasets.source: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue and Gaia DR3 astrometric data for young pulsars
datasets.target: Kinematic reconstruction of natal kick velocities for pulsars with age < 10 Myr

proposal.paperTitle: Kinematic Signatures of Electron-Capture Supernovae in Young Neutron-Star Populations
proposal.paperAbstract: We propose that the natal kick velocity distribution of young neutron stars serves as a primary observable signature distinguishing electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) from iron core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Leveraging the gravitational tug-boat mechanism, we demonstrate that ECSNe produce significantly lower kicks (< 50 km/s) due to reduced asymmetric mass ejection. By analyzing the proper motions of young pulsars (< 10 Myr), we identify a low-velocity subpopulation consistent with ECS origins, providing a statistical method to isolate these rare events in Galactic surveys.
proposal.methods: 1. Select a sample of young radio pulsars (characteristic age < 10 Myr) with precise proper motion measurements from Gaia and VLBI. 2. Correct for Solar motion and Galactic potential to derive peculiar velocities. 3. Compare the observed velocity distribution with bimodal population synthesis models incorporating low-kick (ECS) and high-kick (CCS) components. 4. Identify the fraction of low-velocity pulsars attributable to ECSNe.

baselines: Single-component Maxwellian kick distribution (standard CCSN model)
Bimodal kick distribution with fixed ECS fraction (Stevenson et al. 2022)
metrics: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistic for velocity distribution fit
Fraction of pulsars with v_kick < 50 km/s
Bayesian evidence ratio for bimodal vs unimodal models
experiments.design: Statistical analysis of the transverse velocity distribution of young pulsars. We will test whether a bimodal distribution (representing ECS and CCS channels) provides a significantly better fit than a single-component distribution. Support for the hypothesis requires a statistically significant low-velocity peak (< 50 km/s) that cannot be explained by projection effects or selection biases.

proposal.results: We expect to find a distinct low-velocity component in the young pulsar population, comprising approximately 10-20% of the sample, consistent with the predicted rate of ECSNe. This component will show kick velocities predominantly below 50 km/s, distinguishing it from the broader, higher-velocity distribution of iron core-collapse remnants. Failure to detect this low-velocity peak would challenge the standard ECS kick models or suggest that ECSNe are rarer than currently predicted.

findings.issue: The proposal relies on the Crab pulsar as a canonical ECSN example (implied by ref 1802.05274), but recent high-precision astrometry suggests its kick velocity is ~160 km/s, which contradicts the <50 km/s threshold proposed for ECSNe. This specific counter-example undermines the claim that all or most ECSNe produce such low kicks.
findings.checkedWith: arxiv_search: 'electron-capture supernovae Crab pulsar proper motion kick velocity low mass progenitor'

findings.issue: The proposal assumes a clean bimodal distribution (<50 km/s for ECS vs >200 km/s for CCS). However, evidence from population synthesis (e.g., arXiv:1805.11100) and observational constraints (arXiv:2107.04251) indicates that the 'low-kick' channel may have a broader distribution or overlap with the lower tail of standard CCSN kicks, making a hard 50 km/s cutoff physically unjustified and statistically fragile.
findings.checkedWith: arxiv_search: 'electron-capture supernovae neutron star kick velocity < 50 km/s observational evidence'

findings.issue: The proposal fails to account for selection biases in young pulsar samples. Young pulsars are often found in dense environments or associated with bright SNRs where proper motion measurements are difficult. The 'missing' low-velocity pulsars might be an observational artifact rather than a physical signature.
findings.checkedWith: arxiv_search: 'electron-capture supernovae natal kick velocity distribution young pulsars bimodal'

requiredChanges: Remove the rigid <50 km/s cutoff for ECSNe; adopt a probabilistic kick distribution model that allows for overlap with low-kick CCSNe, citing the broader range of possible ECS kicks.
Address the Crab pulsar counter-example explicitly. If the Crab is an ECSN candidate with a higher kick, explain how the model accommodates this outlier or revise the classification criteria.
Include a detailed analysis of selection biases in Gaia/VLBI data for young pulsars, specifically quantifying how detection limits might skew the observed velocity distribution toward higher values.

proposal.problemStatement: Distinguishing electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) from iron core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in young neutron-star populations requires accounting for overlapping kick velocity distributions and observational selection biases. A rigid velocity cutoff is insufficient; instead, we need a probabilistic framework that accommodates the full range of ECS kicks, including outliers like the Crab pulsar, while quantifying how detection limits skew observed velocity distributions.
proposal.rationale: ECSNe originate from super asymptotic giant branch stars (8-10 solar masses) with degenerate O-Ne-Mg cores. The gravitational tug-boat mechanism dictates that natal kicks scale with asymmetric mass ejection; ECSNe typically have lower ejecta masses and reduced asymmetries, producing lower average kicks. However, hydrodynamical simulations show that ECS kicks follow a broad distribution with significant overlap with low-kick CCSNe, rather than exhibiting a sharp cutoff. The Crab pulsar, potentially an ECSN remnant, demonstrates that some ECS events can produce moderate kicks (~150 km/s). Selection biases in proper motion surveys further complicate identification, as low-velocity pulsars may be underrepresented due to detection limits favoring high-transverse-velocity objects. A probabilistic mixture model, combined with careful bias correction, provides a robust statistical signature for distinguishing ECS contributions.
proposal.technicalDetails: We will analyze the transverse velocity distribution of young radio pulsars (< 10 Myr) using a Bayesian hierarchical mixture model that allows for overlapping kick distributions between ECS and CCS channels. Rather than imposing a rigid <50 km/s cutoff, we model ECS kicks as a Maxwellian distribution with scale parameter σ_ECS ≈ 30-80 km/s and CCS kicks as σ_CCS ≈ 200-300 km/s, with mixing fraction f_ECS treated as a free parameter. We explicitly account for selection biases by modeling the detection probability as a function of transverse velocity, incorporating Gaia magnitude limits and VLBI sensitivity thresholds. The Crab pulsar is included as a known outlier to test model flexibility.

proposal.paperTitle: Probabilistic Kinematic Signatures of Electron-Capture Supernovae in Young Neutron-Star Populations with Selection Bias Correction
proposal.paperAbstract: We propose a probabilistic framework for distinguishing electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) from iron core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in young neutron-star populations, addressing limitations of rigid velocity cutoffs. Leveraging the gravitational tug-boat mechanism, we model ECS kicks as a broad Maxwellian distribution (σ ≈ 30-80 km/s) that overlaps with low-kick CCSNe, accommodating outliers such as the Crab pulsar. By analyzing proper motions of young pulsars (< 10 Myr) from Gaia and VLBI, we implement a Bayesian hierarchical mixture model that simultaneously infers kick distribution parameters and corrects for selection biases arising from detection limits. Our approach quantifies the ECS fraction while accounting for observational incompleteness at low transverse velocities, providing a statistically robust method to isolate these rare events in Galactic surveys.
proposal.methods: 1. Select a sample of young radio pulsars (characteristic age < 10 Myr) with precise proper motion measurements from Gaia DR3 and VLBI, including known outliers like the Crab pulsar. 2. Model selection biases by computing detection probabilities as functions of transverse velocity, accounting for Gaia magnitude limits (G < 20.7) and VLBI flux density thresholds. 3. Implement a Bayesian hierarchical mixture model with two Maxwellian kick components (ECS and CCS) and a free mixing fraction, allowing for distribution overlap. 4. Use Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling to infer posterior distributions for σ_ECS, σ_CCS, and f_ECS, marginalizing over distance and age uncertainties. 5. Validate the model by testing whether it can recover known ECS candidates (e.g., Crab pulsar) within the inferred ECS distribution tail.

baselines: Single-component Maxwellian kick distribution (standard CCSN model without ECS channel)
Bimodal kick distribution with rigid <50 km/s ECS cutoff (previous approach)
Bimodal distribution without selection bias correction
metrics: Bayesian evidence ratio for bimodal vs unimodal models
Posterior distribution of ECS mixing fraction f_ECS
Goodness-of-fit via posterior predictive checks on velocity distribution
Recovery rate of known ECS candidates (e.g., Crab pulsar) within credible intervals
experiments.design: Statistical analysis of the transverse velocity distribution of young pulsars with explicit bias correction. We compare three models: (1) single-component CCS-only, (2) bimodal with rigid cutoff, and (3) bimodal with overlapping distributions and bias correction. Support for the hypothesis requires that model (3) provides significantly better Bayesian evidence than alternatives, recovers the Crab pulsar within the ECS component's credible interval, and yields an ECS fraction consistent with stellar evolution predictions (10-20%). Failure to detect a distinct low-kick component after bias correction would challenge the standard ECS kick models or suggest that ECSNe are rarer than predicted.

proposal.results: We expect the probabilistic mixture model with bias correction to reveal a low-kick component comprising 10-20% of young pulsars, with σ_ECS ≈ 50 km/s and significant overlap with the low-velocity tail of the CCS distribution. The Crab pulsar should fall within the upper tail of the ECS distribution, demonstrating that ECS kicks are not universally low but follow a broad distribution. Selection bias correction will increase the inferred ECS fraction by 20-30% compared to naive analyses, as low-velocity pulsars are systematically underdetected. If the bimodal model does not significantly outperform the single-component model after accounting for biases, this would suggest either that ECS kicks are indistinguishable from low-kick CCSNe or that the ECS channel is less common than current stellar evolution models predict.
